content: === Introduction ===

Ackerman syndrome or interstitial granulomatous dermatitis is a familial syndrome of fused molar roots with a single canal (taurodontism), hypotrichosis, full upper lip without a cupid's bow, thickened and wide philtrum, and occasional juvenile glaucoma.[1][2][3]
It was described by James L. Ackerman, A. Leon Ackerman, and A. Bernard Ackerman.[4]
=== Signs and symptoms ===
<info> Distinct facial features: full upper lip, absence of cupid's bow, thick philtrum
<info> Increased pigmentation of finger joints
<info> Clinodactyly of fifth finger.[5]
